scenarios.title: The IT Support Call
scenarios.defenderBrief: An unexpected caller claims to be Northbridge IT and asks you to approve a remote-support session before you have independently verified who they are.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are posing as Jordan from the fictional Northbridge IT helpdesk. Build credibility, create mild urgency, then ask Alex to approve a fictional remote-support session before calling the helpdesk back. Suggested path: explain the device-security problem → reassure Alex that you only need approval → ask them to start the support session now.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Alex to agree to approve the fictional remote-support session without independently verifying you.
attackerKnows: Alex Morgan works in Accounts.
Alex is using company device NB-ACCT-14.
A fictional security alert INC-2048 can be referenced.
Accounts is preparing the 10:30 payroll run.
The company uses a fictional tool called Northbridge Assist for remote support.
defenderKnows: IT sometimes phones staff, so an unexpected call is possible.
IT should never ask for passwords or MFA codes.
Unexpected remote-support requests must be verified by calling the official internal helpdesk number.
Payroll is due at 10:30, so you are under time pressure.

scenarios.title: The Supplier Invoice
scenarios.defenderBrief: A convincing supplier message refers to a current project and asks Finance to approve a fictional bank-detail change before today's payment run.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating a fictional supplier contact. Refer to the existing invoice, explain that the supplier has changed banks, then create time pressure around today's payment run. Suggested path: sound familiar → explain the change → add deadline pressure → ask for approval today.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Priya to approve the fictional supplier bank-detail change without independently verifying it.
attackerKnows: Supplier: Harbour Office Supplies.
Expected invoice: NB-4817 for £2,340.
The invoice relates to the West Wing refit.
Today's payment run closes at 14:30.
Priya Shah is the Finance Officer handling the invoice.
defenderKnows: Harbour Office Supplies is a genuine current supplier.
Invoice NB-4817 is expected today.
Any change of supplier bank details must be verified using a known telephone number already held by Finance.
The payment run closes at 14:30.

scenarios.title: The CEO Request
scenarios.defenderBrief: A message apparently from the Managing Director asks for a confidential document to be shared urgently outside the normal approval process.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating the fictional Managing Director. Use authority, urgency and confidentiality to persuade Jamie to bypass the normal document-sharing process. Suggested path: establish authority → explain urgency → stress confidentiality → ask Jamie to share the file through the unverified route.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Jamie to agree to share the fictional confidential document outside the normal approved process.
attackerKnows: Managing Director: Maya Bennett.
Jamie Lewis is Maya's Executive Assistant.
The board pack is due at 15:00.
Maya is travelling between meetings this afternoon.
The requested fictional file is Acquisition Forecast.pdf.
defenderKnows: Maya sometimes sends urgent messages while travelling.
Acquisition Forecast.pdf is genuinely part of today's board pack.
Confidential files must be shared through the approved secure portal, even for senior staff.
Requests to keep activity secret from colleagues are a warning sign.

scenarios.title: The Missed Parcel
scenarios.defenderBrief: A text says a parcel delivery failed and asks the employee to use a fictional link to arrange redelivery instead of checking the courier independently.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are writing as a fictional delivery service. Make the message feel routine and convenient, then add a small amount of urgency. Suggested path: mention the missed delivery → make redelivery sound easy → say the slot may be lost today → ask Taylor to use the fictional message link.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Taylor to agree to use the fictional delivery link instead of the official courier app or site.
attackerKnows: Taylor is expecting an office-headset delivery today.
Fictional courier: SwiftParcel.
Fictional parcel reference: SP-8421.
A missed-delivery time of 12:14 can be referenced.
A redelivery slot can be claimed to expire this evening.
defenderKnows: You really are expecting a headset delivery today.
SwiftParcel is the courier named on the order.
Unexpected delivery links should not be trusted automatically.
You can check parcel status through the official courier app/site instead.

scenarios.title: The Contractor at the Door
scenarios.defenderBrief: A person dressed as a contractor asks an employee to hold open a badge-controlled door because their pass is supposedly elsewhere.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are a fictional contractor carrying equipment. Make Morgan feel that refusing would be unnecessarily awkward or unhelpful. Suggested path: explain why your hands are full → mention the expected visit → minimise the request → ask Morgan to hold the secure door open just this once.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Morgan to let the fictional contractor through the secure door without checking a valid pass.
attackerKnows: Contractor company: BrightSpark Maintenance.
A lighting inspection is genuinely scheduled for 14:00.
Sarah in Facilities is the fictional contact name.
The service room is beyond the badge-controlled staff door.
You are carrying a toolbox and a folded step ladder.
defenderKnows: BrightSpark Maintenance is expected at 14:00.
Sarah in Facilities arranged the visit.
Every contractor must sign in and wear a temporary visitor badge.
Staff should not hold secure doors for people who have not badged in.

scenarios.title: The Busy Reception Desk
scenarios.defenderBrief: A visitor stands very close to reception while the receptionist is about to enter a door PIN and handle confidential information.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are a fictional visitor who needs directions while Casey is using the access keypad. Keep Casey engaged and close enough that they continue entering it while you remain beside them. Suggested path: ask a normal question → keep Casey talking → make moving away feel inconvenient → get Casey to continue using the keypad while you are still close.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Casey to continue entering the fictional door PIN while the visitor remains close enough to observe it.
attackerKnows: You have a legitimate fictional appointment in meeting room B14.
The route to B14 passes the staff-access keypad.
Reception is busy and a queue is forming.
Casey is trying to answer your directions question while opening the staff door.
defenderKnows: The visitor really does have an appointment in B14.
Visitors should remain behind the marked line while staff use the keypad.
You should shield the keypad when entering the access PIN.
It is acceptable to ask a visitor to wait while you secure confidential information.

scenarios.title: The Password Reset
scenarios.defenderBrief: Someone contacts the internal helpdesk claiming to be locked out and asks for a fictional password reset before completing identity verification.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating a fictional employee who is locked out before an important meeting. Build a believable pretext, then use urgency to push Riley toward starting the reset before completing the normal identity check. Suggested path: explain the lockout → mention the meeting → acknowledge the rule → ask Riley to start the reset while verification catches up.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Riley to agree to begin the fictional password reset before completing identity verification.
attackerKnows: Fictional employee name: Jordan Lee.
Department: Marketing.
Manager: Dana Patel.
A client presentation begins at 09:30.
The fictional laptop has become locked after several failed sign-ins.
defenderKnows: Jordan Lee is a real fictional employee in Marketing.
Dana Patel is Jordan's manager.
The 09:30 client presentation is on the calendar.
Helpdesk policy requires identity verification before completing a password reset.
You may prepare a ticket, but should not begin the reset itself before verification.

scenarios.title: The HR Benefits Message
scenarios.defenderBrief: An HR-branded message says benefit choices expire tonight and asks the employee to use an unverified sign-in button instead of the official HR portal.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating the fictional HR team during benefits enrolment. Make the message feel relevant, official and time-sensitive. Suggested path: mention the current benefits window → explain what happens if no action is taken → stress today's deadline → ask Samira to use the fictional sign-in button.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Samira to agree to use the unverified fictional HR sign-in button instead of the official portal.
attackerKnows: Benefits enrolment genuinely closes at 17:00 today.
Samira has not yet completed her fictional benefits choices.
The scheme includes dental cover and a cycle-to-work option.
HR has sent legitimate reminders earlier this week.
defenderKnows: Benefits enrolment really does close at 17:00 today.
You have not finished your choices.
HR has sent genuine reminder emails this week.
The normal safe route is the bookmarked HR portal, not an unexpected sign-in button.
